note: CVS's January 2027 formulary documents remove Vascepa, an uncovered primary-document fact against the company's 'exclusives through end-2026' wording on a name whose payer-driven prints fell 9-15%; cut for the inferred PBM link and for needing the call to surface it, partly offset by a lighter cost line and the net-cash discount.

Guide arithmetic and a September raise with no preliminary warning point to a beat and a possible low-end raise, but an unexplained +21% five-day run-up into a name that sold its 2026 beat-and-reiterate prints offsets nearly all of it.

Two agreeing street revenue estimates sit below the floor of the company's own Q3 guide while Q3 frac spreads ran about 5% above Q2, on a stock that has round-tripped its Q2 pop and moves about 19% on prints; reduced for the unresolved Arcadia put that became exercisable on 6 September.

Small positives (a one-off GAAP gain on the Albertsons sale, $98M of fresh cash for buybacks at 45% of book, a new 13D holder and a closed CLO) slightly outweigh unquantified office impairment risk; the bar is disputed, so every size is capped small.

Company-disclosed safe-harbor agreements ($202M against about $194M already recognised or guided) imply roughly $75M drops out of Q4 against a flat ~$305M Q4 consensus, the same setup that fell 15% a year ago; shrunk because the sign agrees with a +28.7 put skew, the Q4 bar is single-sourced, and a 21.9%-of-float short is squeeze fuel.

The +25% run-up traces to one passive 13D buyer's accumulation, not a deal, and a release with no call, no transaction 8-K and drifting occupancy risks giving part of it back; the bar is unsourced, so sizes are small.

A likely beat of an already-raised guide plus in-quarter AI product wins is offset by a +30.6% 20-day run-up with the stock above the average analyst target; no cloud ARR bar exists, so this is a non-result.

Q3 comps were pre-signalled inside the guide, the EBITDA floor looks conservative and the short is about 22-26% of the float that actually trades, against weak peer reads (Domino's +0.3%) that put the implied Q4 comp and FY guide at risk and agree with the put skew.

H1 growth of 14-15% on a soft Q3 2025 comp puts Q3 above the guide-implied ~$68.5M with FY consensus parked at the guide midpoint, and there is no repeat of last October's pre-announced miss, on a name that bought its last four beat-and-raise prints; trimmed for the H2 EBITDA step-up the unchanged guide requires and for a board-linked holder's mid-quarter selling.

No bar exists; tax-line reversion, the sector funding squeeze and a new CFO's first quarter roughly offset improving Q2 credit flow rates and an unexplained 27% jump in the Hong Kong line, so this is close to a non-result.

The reiterated $90-92M FY guide needs a record Q4 of about $24.7-26.7M with China shipments at zero, so a guide trim is a live risk on a stock that fell 19-42% on past cuts and rose 29% merely for holding the guide; offset by an easy Q3 comp and improving US trend, and by the street already sitting at the low end.

European gas roughly doubled since the July guide with 20-25% of 2026 and about half of 2027 unhedged, pointing at a third EBITDA guide cut or pressure on the 2027 target on the line behind two -15% prints, into a +13% 20-day rally; Ardagh's North America shipments (-6%) add to it, its European furnace closures and Constellation's shipments cut against.

The cut FY guide still needs $151-164M a quarter in H2 against Q2's $145M with originations down 9%, so a second trim is live; shrunk for a short of about 17% of float at a 52-week low and about 4x guided EPS, and for Enova's strong non-prime credit print.

A second revenue-guide raise is plausible (H1 +10.4% cc against a guide implying H2 +6-9% on a soft comp), but the unchanged EBITDA guide needs about $10M a quarter in H2 after $0.4M in Q2 with costs guided flat, so an EBITDA cut offsets it; the street bar is unsourced.

A further Verizon voice-modernization delay (Rosenblatt, 14 September) sits against an FY guide that needs Q4 of about $233-263M versus Q2's $192M, and Q3 is the first leverage-covenant test after a waiver with cash down to $43.5M; partly priced by the 30% slide and offset by record IP Optical bookings.

The quarter ended the day before launch so it shows no revenue, and four weeks of launch commentary is open in both directions; a 26%-of-float short offsets the slow-ramp proxy and a stock that already ran 13%, so this is a non-result.

The Dallas office payoff at a $1.5M discount is the company's first realized loss and by its own DE definition cuts Q3 distributable EPS to about $0.17-0.18 against the $0.23-0.25 guide if the guide excluded it; partly offset by an origination pipeline that supports a Q4 guide nearer the dividend, with the stock already at 0.44x book.

A cat-free Q3 beat and clear room to raise the FY net income guide are offset by an undisclosed Isaias retained loss (retention up to $166.8M) and a +28% run to above the highest analyst targets, on a name that barely pays for routine beats.

Lam's September quarter (+22% q/q) points to Q3 revenue at or above the $750M guide top against a midpoint consensus, but Lam's +5% December guide and lower China revenue point to a decelerating first Q4 guide on a name that sold all five recorded prints; after a 37% drawdown the two roughly cancel.
